newsitem.title: UK: Med Aframax tankers active, most rates flat.
newsitem.headline: Med Aframax tankers active, most rates flat.

text.p: The cross-Mediterranean market was active on Wednesday with some some nine Aframax cargoes fixed, brokers said.
The rate for 80,000 tonne vessels was a firm W125, with scope for the market to rise further if demand continues, they added.
"Med Aframaxes are the market to watch. It's hotting up quite a lot at the moment," one broker said.

The Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) sector showed modest signs of life after a dull period. "I've seen a bit more business in the last 24 hours but we need to see it sustained before anyone gets too excited," another broker said.
The Mideast/west market, which has been dormant recently, saw two fixtures, the Evelyn Maersk and the Murex, both 285,000 tonne cargoes at W55 to the U.S. Gulf for Saudi Arabia's Vela.
The Mideast/Japan rate was assessed at W65/68, with one vessel rumoured done at the higher level, while VLCCs to Singapore sagged at W60.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were steady to slightly firmer at W67.5, with Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne ships) at W90.
In the transatlantic sector, the 270,000 tonne Hellespont Paradise was done at W67.5 for Hess on a Mongstad/St Croix voyage.
U.K./Cont Aframax rates meanwhile dipped to W120 from W125 on lower enquiry.

The often turbulent Caribs/upcoast remained unusually tranquil, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes unchanged at W170 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W190, brokers said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
